authority_note: Nate authorised this run directly. No packet was admitted. Evidence only — nothing promoted, no verdict recorded, no write outside this directory.

environment.browser: real Google Chrome via Claude browser extension
environment.keystrokes: genuine OS-level Tab keypresses, not synthesized KeyboardEvents

headline: Real-Chrome keyboard traversal is achievable from this side. Literal 390 CSS px is NOT, for either toolset. Two of six pages completed a valid traversal; four did not and are recorded as UNVERIFIED rather than clean.

evidence: resize_window to 390 -> innerWidth clamped to 500 (macOS Chrome minimum window width)
at 500 CSS px the max-width:480px mobile breakpoint does NOT engage
document.documentElement.style.zoom does not move clientWidth or matchMedia
DevTools shortcut cmd+alt+i does not reach browser chrome from the extension
viewport_390_finding.conclusion: Window resize cannot reach 390. Only DevTools device emulation can, and that requires a human hand. Codex's split (390 geometry via in-app browser, real keyboard at desktop) is a rational response to the same limit, not an oversight. Recommend recording the 390-keyboard gap as an ACCEPTED TOOLING LIMIT rather than an open defect.

our-story.reason: Chrome lost OS-level window focus; keypresses did not reach the page. Zero stops is an INVALID measurement, not a clean result.

carob-story.reason: same OS focus loss; retried once with a verified non-interactive click at (190,120) and still recorded 0 stops

established: Real OS-level Tab keypresses do move focus in-page once Chrome holds window focus — the capability Codex's in-app injector lacks.
On homepage and shop, 60 Tab presses produced 59 focus stops with ZERO leaks into the closed cart dialog. Focus containment holds under real keyboard.

The closed cart dialog carries inert (attribute AND property) plus aria-hidden=true on all four pages loaded. This is applied at RUNTIME by mock-cart.js and is absent from the static HTML, so no static analysis can confirm it — this run does.
No zero-size or offscreen focus stops on either validly traversed page.

NOT_established.claim: 5 homepage controls focus without a visible focus ring
NOT_established.status: WITHDRAWN — measurement artifact, do not act on it
NOT_established.why: The initial reading came from computed style sampled inside a focusin handler, which may precede style recalculation. The deterministic cross-check was also inconclusive: programmatic .focus() reported changedOnFocus:[] for ALL 19 controls including ones observed to show rings under real Tab, because these pages use :focus-visible, which programmatic focus cannot trigger. Neither method can reliably detect the indicator. Requires visual confirmation by screenshot while a control holds real keyboard focus.
NOT_established.recommended_next: Screenshot each focus stop under real Tab and inspect visually. Not done here.

NOT_established: Keyboard traversal at literal 390 CSS px — impossible with available tooling, see viewport_390_finding.
Escape-to-close and focus-return-to-trigger on the cart dialog — not exercised.
residual_risk: Four of six pages are unverified. Any six-page keyboard claim must not rely on this record.
Traversal was at 500 CSS px, which is DESKTOP layout — the 480px mobile breakpoint does not engage. This does not substitute for mobile keyboard verification.
Chrome window focus proved intermittent across navigations, so a full six-page sweep needs the window kept frontmost throughout.
